sources.title: SolidGoldFX Fuzzbox - Vintage/Modern Fuzz | Effects Database
sources.excerpt: Published on September 20, 2026 SolidGoldFX fuzz pedal Information The SolidGoldFX Fuzzbox is a modern take on the Tone Bender Mk II, the circuit developed in mid-1960s England that went on to define the sound of British rock. That original was thick and harmonically rich, and responsive enough to a player's touch that it worked as an extension of the guitar rather than simply a distortion, cleaning up as the volume knob rolled back and opening into singing sustain when pushed. It reached records and stages through players including Jimmy Page, Jeff Beck, and Mick Ronson. Rather than copying one particular vintage unit, the Fuzzbox rebuilds the idea around carefully selected low-gain silicon transistors, which hold onto the warmth and harmonic texture of the original design while behaving consistently from one pedal to the next. On top of that it exposes the two variables that most define how a fuzz reacts but are usually fixed inside the box: the bias of the circuit and the voltage feeding it. Bias adjusts the operating point of the third transistor, which has a large effect on both voice and feel. Wound down it produces a gated, splatty texture with more aggression; wound up it smooths out into a fuller sound with more conventional sustain. Sag simulates a dying battery across a range of roughly 9 V down to 5 V. Fully counterclockwise, at full voltage, the pedal stays tight, punchy, and stable; as it advances and the voltage drops, the attack softens, compression builds, and the circuit falls into the starved behavior associated with old fuzz tones. Between them the pedal covers tight and articulate through to sputtering and collapsing without falling apart musically. Alongside those, Level sets output and Fuzz sets the amount of saturation, opening from a gritty, more open drive at lower settings into thick, compressed, sustaining fuzz further up. In practice the two interact. Sag and Bias both wound up gives a buzzsaw texture with a torn, Velcro-like edge; backing Sag off reduces the starved-battery behavior and returns sustain. Bias set low leaves a gnarly, heavily saturated fuzz that thins out at the bottom, and bringing it back toward the middle of its travel restores the low end without giving up the thickness. A switch selects how the pedal's input stage is wired. Vintage mode connects straight to the fuzz circuit with no buffer, giving the purest signal path and the rawest, most immediate response, and leaving the pedal maximally sensitive to the guitar's volume control and pickups so gain and texture can be steered from the instrument itself. Modern mode places a buffer on the input for a smoother, more controlled response with a subtle lift in the low end, which holds up more consistently across different guitars, amps, and pedalboards, and notably gets along better with a wah or other effects placed in front of it. Controls Level: Sets the overall output level Fuzz: Sets the amount of fuzz and saturation, from a more open, gritty drive to thick, sustaining, more compressed fuzz Bias: Adjusts the operating point of the third transistor; lower settings give a gated, splatty and more aggressive texture, higher settings a smoother and fuller sound with more traditional sustain. Around the middle of its travel it brings low end back into a sound that has gone too fuzzy to hold its bottom Sag: Simulates a dying battery, roughly 9 V down to 5 V; tight, punchy, and stable at full voltage, softening the attack and increasing compression into starved behavior as voltage drops Vintage / Modern: Selects an unbuffered direct connection to the fuzz circuit, or a buffered input with a fuller low end and better compatibility with a wah and other pedals placed before it Footswitch: Engages or bypasses the effect Connections Input: Instrument input Output: Output to the amplifier Power: 9 to 18 V DC Technical Specifications Circuit Type: Silicon, based on the Tone Bender Mk II, using low-gain silicon transistors Input Stage: Switchable between unbuffered (Vintage) and buffered (Modern) Sag Range: Approximately 9 V to 5 V simulated supply Power Requirements: 9 to 18 V DC, 20 mA Warranty: Limited three-year warranty from date of purchase Highlights Tone Bender Mk II Reworked: Keeps the character and touch response of the original without copying one specific vintage unit Low-Gain Silicon Transistors: Warmth and harmonic texture of the classic design with consistent behavior between units Bias on the Third Transistor: Moves the pedal from gated and splatty to smooth and sustaining Sag as a Control: Puts the voltage starve of a dying battery under the player's hand rather than leaving it to chance Vintage and Modern Input Stages: An unbuffered path for maximum sensitivity to the guitar, or a buffered one that plays well with a wah in front Wide Voltage Range: Runs on anything from 9 to 18 V DC Video all | by manufacturer | not by manufacturer Date ▼▲ Maker ▼▲ Video ▼▲ Time ▼▲ 2026-09-23 Solid Gold Sound Labs RJ Ronquillo Plays | SolidGoldFX Fuzzbox 0:41 2026-09-16 Solid Gold Sound Labs RJ Ronquillo Plays | SolidGoldFX Fuzzbox 0:34 2026-09-16 Solid Gold Sound Labs Walt Druce Plays the SGFX Fuzzbox 0:33 2026-09-16 R.J. sources.title: New Pedal: SolidGoldFX Fuzzbox | Delicious Audio
sources.excerpt: Updated Sep. 15, 2026 | by Paolo De Gregorio The SGFX Fuzzbox is a modern evolution of one of the most iconic British fuzz circuits ever conceived—the Tone Bender Mk II. Born in mid-sixties England, the original design helped shape the raw, high-gain landscape of early rock in the hands of legends like Jimmy Page, Jeff Beck, and Mick Ronson. It wasn’t merely distortion; it functioned as a living extension of the guitar, cleaning up organically with a roll of the volume knob and blooming into singing, harmonic sustain when pushed. Instead of chasing an unyielding, museum-piece clone, the Fuzzbox focuses entirely on feel. At its heart are carefully selected low-gain silicon transistors engineered to deliver the warmth, bite, and touch sensitivity of vintage gear, but with the reliability and range required for contemporary setups. The pedal relies heavily on tactile control to bridge vintage grit with modern utility: Vintage/Modern Toggle: The Vintage setting provides the raw, immediate response of a classic Mk II, maximizing direct guitar-to-circuit interaction for explosive attack. Flipping to Modern smooths out the input, introduces a fuller low-end presence, and ensures seamless compatibility with buffers, wah pedals, and crowded boards. Bias Control: Adjusts the operating point of the third transistor, shifting the texture from a tight, focused grind to a softer, more saturated crunch. Sag Control: Mimics the behavior of a fading battery by scaling internal voltage down from 9V to 5V, yielding a yielding, naturally compressed attack. The result is a deeply expressive, highly responsive stompbox that honors classic British fire while giving players total command over their tone.
